title: Senior Data Analyst Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Convert a senior data analyst salary from hourly to annual using the 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, award rates, and Fair Work benchmarks for Australian workers.
salarySummary: A senior data analyst salary often exceeds the national minimum wage; using the 38-hour week, an hourly rate of $50 gives an annual gross of $98,800 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a senior data analyst in Australia?
faqs.a: There is no single mandated rate, as senior data analyst salaries vary by industry, experience, and location. However, many roles fall under the Professional Employees Award or are above-award. For a benchmark, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported average weekly ordinary-time earnings for full-time adults at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026), which equates to about $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. Actual senior data analyst salaries can be higher, often ranging from $50 to $80 per hour depending on the employer.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $60 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $118,560 gross per year. If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Remember that this calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: Does superannuation come on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Yes. The super guarantee requires your employer to contribute 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, on top of your base salary. For a $118,560 annual salary, that adds an extra $14,227.20 in super contributions (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). This is not deducted from your pay; it is paid separately by your employer.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Senior Data Analyst Salary in Australia

If you are evaluating a **senior data analyst salary** offer or negotiating a contract, knowing how to convert an hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. In Australia, most full-time roles are based on a 38-hour week, and the Fair Work Ombudsman provides clear guidance on minimum wages and award rates. This article explains the conversion formula, distinguishes between the National Minimum Wage and award rates, and shows how tax and superannuation affect your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The standard calculation for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, if your hourly rate is $55, your annual gross is $55 × 38 × 52 = $108,680. This formula works for any hourly rate, but it assumes you work the same number of hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time, simply replace 38 with your actual weekly hours.

### Fortnightly Pay and Weekly Equivalents

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same $55 per hour example, weekly pay is $55 × 38 = $2,090, so fortnightly pay is $4,180. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers expressed per fortnight.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates vs. Senior Data Analyst Salaries

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, a **senior data analyst salary** is almost always above these minimums. Many data analysts are covered by the Professional Employees Award, which sets higher minimum rates for qualified professionals. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database contains the exact minimum rates for each classification.

For a realistic benchmark, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reported average weekly ordinary-time earnings for full-time adults at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That equates to roughly $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. Senior data analyst roles often pay above this average, especially in industries like finance, technology, and consulting. Actual salaries can range from $100,000 to $150,000 per year, depending on experience and location.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income (reductions may apply for low incomes). For a $108,680 annual salary, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be roughly $25,000–$26,000, leaving a take-home pay of about $82,000–$83,000. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more detailed estimate.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must contribute superannuation at 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For a $108,680 salary, the super contribution is $13,041.60 per year. This is not included in your take-home pay but builds your retirement savings. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Casual Loading and Award Coverage

If you work as a casual senior data analyst, you may be entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) list the correct rates for each award. Always check your award or enterprise agreement, as some employers offer above-award rates.

### Putting It All Together

To convert a **senior data analyst salary** from hourly to annual:

1. Confirm your hourly rate (base, excluding casual loading if you are permanent).
2. Multiply by 38 (or your actual weekly hours).
3. Multiply by 52 to get annual gross.
4. Add 12% super on top (employer contribution).
5. Estimate tax and Medicare to find take-home pay.

For example, a $60 per hour rate gives:
- Annual gross: $60 × 38 × 52 = $118,560
- Fortnightly gross: $60 × 38 × 2 = $4,560
- Super (12%): $14,227.20
- Estimated tax + Medicare: ~$30,000–$31,000
- Take-home: ~$87,000–$88,000

Remember that this is an estimate. Actual pay may vary due to overtime, allowances, salary sacrifice, or enterprise agreements. For precise figures, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [reference tables](/data) or consult your employer.

### Why This Matters

Understanding the conversion helps you compare job offers, negotiate salaries, and plan your budget. Whether you are a senior data analyst looking at a contract role or a permanent position, the same principles apply. The key is to know your base hourly rate, the hours you will work, and whether you are covered by an award. The Fair Work Commission and ABS provide reliable data, while recruiter surveys can offer market insights but may not reflect legal minimums.

For more information, see our guides on [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).
